title: Quantum embeddings for machine learning
scope: Main I-III embedding/objective/measurement; mainIV-VI experiment and resource limitations; AppendixA definitions/B classification-v-state discrimination/C fidelity/D1-D3 Helstrom and pair averaging. Reference list read only as leads, not source verification of cited works.

findings.locator: p2-p3 SectionsI-II; p8 AppA; p9 AppC
findings.claim: Binary quantum data embedding has a linear-observable classifier; fidelity output uses difference of class-mean density operators. Its class-balanced linear-risk expression is negative HS separation under the source normalization convention; not a CE/Macro or generalization theorem.
HS separation is known kernel mean discrepancy for fidelity kernel. Merely adding class-separation/metric learning is not newT.

findings.locator: p5 SectionIV final paragraph; p6 Conclusion
findings.claim: The numerical demonstration does not establish superiority over classical ML. Small-circuit simulation here cannot inherit classically inaccessible many-qubit claims.

findings.locator: p10 AppD2 displayed pure-pair averaging equation, checked against AppD1 sign observable; transfer_audit.py
findings.claim: Literal interchange of taking matrix sign and averaging independently solved pure pairs fails. A one-qubit ensemble gives mixed-sign expectation +0.03701166, pure-pair-sign average -0.03133975. Does not contradict Helstrom theorem or independent mixed-ensemble-copy algorithms.

findings.locator: Current original rmea.py forward; native counterexample in transfer_audit.py
findings.claim: Native logit is fractional signed-utility operator expectation. Identical unweighted token density can yield logits +/-0.999998; uniform-density MMD alone does not characterize that classifier.

findings.locator: transfer_audit.py exact formula plus64 random state-port checks
findings.claim: Fractional and lifted pairwise margin identities are standard linear algebra, not newT or utility. Random state checks do not certify native circuit reachability.

limits: No repository code/supplement replication or hardware complexity theorem validation.
The source has no Eq guaranteeing Macro-F1 for the40-class value-weighted normalized token model.
We reject the proposed naive transfer/proxy, not all metric learning, Helstrom classification or quantum methods.
